newsitem.title: YEMEN: Yemen president launches free zone project.
newsitem.headline: Yemen president launches free zone project.

text.p: Yemen's President Ali Abdullah Saleh laid the foundation stone on Monday for a $500 million project to build the infrastructure of a free zone area in the southern port city of Aden.
Officials hope the work will attract badly needed foreign investment in the impoverished Arab state and revive Aden's past glory as a busy bunkering and services hub.
After the closure of the Suez Canal during the 1967 Middle East war the number of ships calling at the port dropped from 6,000 a year to a current 600.

The contract for the project was awarded in May to the Yemen Investment and Development International Company (YEMINVEST), a consortium which includes Saudi investors of Yemeni origin, the Saudi International Development Co and the U.S Alliance Development Co.

An official announcement by the Yemen Free Zone Public Authority in November said the contract provides for building a new six-quay port with a 16-metre (52 feet) deep navigational channel and a container terminal opposite the existing port.
The contract provides also for an industrial park, a 180- megawatt power station, communications and sewerage networks and administrative offices.
Yemen will receive 25 percent of the revenue starting the first operational year, to be gradually increased to 100 percent by the end of the 25-year contract.
Officials involved in the project told Reuters that building, operations and marketing contracts have been awarded to international companies.
